title: Consumer-directed Medicaid support can improve caregiver wellbeing without proving recipient recovery or durable household security
source_unit: ASPE Cash and Counseling randomized Medicaid caregiver follow-up
geography: United States; Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey Medicaid demonstration

observations.period: Cash and Counseling caregiver follow-up; approximately 10 months after assignment, report published 2005

denominator.unit: published primary informal-caregiver interviews: 1,433 Arkansas, 1,193 Florida, and 1,042 New Jersey

intervention.value: beneficiary randomized to consumer-directed Cash and Counseling support or usual personal-care/home-and-community-based services

control_route.value: beneficiary could adjust service amount, timing, and type, hire a primary caregiver, name a decision maker, or purchase permitted assistive devices/home modifications

caregiver_wellbeing.value: treatment caregivers fared better than controls on at least half of 15 key wellbeing and satisfaction measures

perceived_financial_strain.value: consumer direction alleviated perceived financial strain in all three states, while caregiver household income did not discernibly change

paid_caregiver_health.value: paid treatment-group caregivers showed better outcomes on important emotional-strain and physical-health measures, with effects generally larger than among unpaid treatment caregivers

recipient_and_household_recovery.unit: missing exact paid hours/amount, recipient clinical outcome, employment/earnings, household buffers, long-run persistence, trust, switching, and exit

mechanism.value: A public care program can reduce perceived caregiver strain and improve wellbeing while leaving coordination, unpaid labor, recipient need, and household risk inside the family

observations.method: Structured extraction from the ASPE report How Cash and Counseling Affects Informal Caregivers; randomized assignment, caregiver interview counts, wellbeing, satisfaction, financial-strain, and paid-caregiver health comparisons are kept separate from recipient and household outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: State implementation and outcome measures differ. The public report does not retain caregiver task hours, exact paid amount, recipient clinical outcome, employment/earnings, household buffers, provider alternatives, long-run persistence, trust, collective action, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Primary informal caregivers identified by participating Medicaid beneficiaries in Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey; paid and unpaid treatment caregivers are described, but no pooled beneficiary-caregiver household denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved caregiver wellbeing can coexist with unmet recipient need, new household costs, later service loss, or no change in caregiver income; short-run relief is not durable recovery.

boundary: This record establishes a randomized care-support-to-caregiver-wellbeing segment. It does not establish recipient care completion, long-run household recovery, caregiver employment recovery, trust, action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the published ASPE caregiver report; beneficiary, caregiver, Medicaid, and claims microdata are not retained.
